EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East situation has escalated significantly over the past 24 hours, with the US launching extensive airstrikes against over 80 Iranian military targets, leading to Iranian military casualties and retaliatory strikes against US facilities in the Gulf. US President Trump declared the interim agreement with Iran "over" and threatened further attacks, while Iran vowed to close the Strait of Hormuz and retaliate with double the force if new aggressions occur, causing oil prices to spike and shipping to halt.

IRAN
The United States launched over 80 strikes against Iranian military targets in Bandar Abbas, Sirik, Qeshm, Hormozgan Province, Bushehr (including an aerospace facility, IRGC base, and air force site), Kharg Island, Mahshahr, Dashti, and Choghadak. Targets included air defense systems, coastal surveillance, surface-to-air missiles, anti-ship cruise missile sites, drone launch sites, and over 60 IRGC small boats. These attacks were described by a US official as "four or five times bigger" than previous strikes ten days ago. Iranian state TV released footage showing destruction at Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei's home and office following his assassination.

Eight Iranian Army servicemen were martyred in these attacks in Bandar Abbas and Bushehr, including Captain Ali Moeini from Bushehr Air Base and naval personnel from Bandar Abbas. A Basij fighter was killed by drone shrapnel in Mahshahr, and one person was killed and two injured in Khuzestan Province. Fishermen's boats at Bandar Abbas pier were also reportedly destroyed or burned.

In retaliation, the IRGC claimed to have attacked 85 US military targets at Salman Port, the 5th Naval Region of Bahrain, and Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait, also claiming to have downed an MQ-9 drone. Kuwait confirmed intercepting two ballistic missiles and 13 drones from Iran, reporting no damage or casualties, though power outages due to transmission line disconnections were noted. Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters warned that any support for the US army would be considered a legitimate target.

Iran has adopted a new strategy, threatening to fully close the Strait of Hormuz and strike enemy targets at least twice the number of targets hit in response to any new US attack. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf listed US violations of the memorandum of understanding (MoU), including actions in Hormuz, military threats, attacks in southern Iran, renewed oil sanctions, and Israeli actions in Lebanon, declaring the "era of bullying" over. Ali Akbar Velayati, an advisor to the Supreme Leader, stated the "Axis of Resistance will not remain silent." The Iranian Foreign Ministry condemned the US lifting of the oil sanctions waiver as a violation of the MoU. President Pezeshkian, who shortened his visit to Iraq for Khamenei's funeral, criticized US behavior, equating it to bullying and cheating.

Internally, large crowds attended Khamenei's funeral procession in Najaf and Karbala, Iraq. The dollar price in Iran reached approximately 180,000 Toman, reflecting economic instability. Iran's Civil Aviation Organization denied reports of airport closures in Hormozgan.

ISRAEL
Israeli forces conducted an airstrike in the southern Gaza Strip, eliminating Mohammed Emad Alrahman Abu Taima, a Hamas Nukhba Force commander involved in the October 7, 2023, attack on Kibbutz Nirim. In southern Lebanon, an Oketz canine unit dog was killed by a Hezbollah gunman in Bint Jbeil before the gunman was killed by either the dog's handler or reservists; the IDF is investigating the exact circumstances. Israeli forces also carried out building demolitions in Taybe, southern Lebanon, and an Israeli drone reportedly targeted Nabatieh Al-Fawqa.

In the West Bank, the IDF arrested 20 wanted individuals, including those planning attacks, arms dealers, and Hamas affiliates, and completed a "Mosc" operation in Jenin, searching over 50 buildings. Searches were conducted in Hebron and Kiryat Arba after gunfire, which resulted in a bullet hitting a house.

On the home front, the IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir called for a significant expansion of IDF ranks. President Herzog spoke against societal polarization and emphasized loyalty to the sovereign people. Chairperson of the Knesset Finance Committee Hanoch Milbicki froze 1 billion NIS in rehabilitation funds for the Gaza envelope, drawing protests. The shekel weakened against major foreign currencies due to regional escalation. The door of the Haaretz newspaper office in Tel Aviv was smashed, days after a similar incident at the N12 office, with no arrests. The Israeli consulate in New York was evacuated due to a nearby building collapse risk. Leaked recordings revealed Shin Bet Chief David Zini stating his loyalty to the elected official, sparking debate and criticism. Justice Minister Gideon Sa'ar and Coalition Chairman Ofir Katz called to defy a High Court ruling regarding the State Comptroller appointment. Prime Minister Netanyahu stated on CNN that selling F-35s to Turkey would upset the regional balance. Israeli military and intelligence assessments indicate preparation for a potential new confrontation and even full war with Iran, in "full coordination" with CENTCOM.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, an Israeli drone strike reportedly targeted a car near the Islamic University in Gaza City, killing two individuals. Another drone strike in southern Khan Younis reportedly killed three people and injured seven in a tent. An attempt to smuggle thousands of cigarettes into Gaza via humanitarian aid shipments, concealed in pineapples, was foiled. In the West Bank (Judea and Samaria), Israeli forces arrested 20 wanted persons, including Hamas affiliates, and conducted extensive searches in Jenin, Hebron, Kiryat Arba, and Tulkarm.

LEBANON
A Hezbollah gunman killed an Oketz canine unit dog in Bint Jbeil before being killed by Israeli forces. This incident follows a previous engagement where a Hezbollah operative seriously wounded an Israeli reservist in the same area. The IDF conducted a series of building demolitions in the Shiite village of Taybe in southern Lebanon. An Israeli drone was reported on a building's roof in Tulin, southern Lebanon, and another drone reportedly targeted Nabatieh Al-Fawqa. A Lebanese official expressed reservations about participating in a sixth round of negotiations in Rome, demanding Israel withdraw from two "pilot areas" as per framework agreements. US President Trump indicated he believes Israel will withdraw from southern Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Syrian President Ahmed al-Shara arrived in Ankara for the NATO summit, with US President Trump suggesting that Syria could assist with Hezbollah and be removed from the US list of state sponsors of terrorism. In Iraq, millions of mourners participated in the funeral procession for Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei in Najaf and Karbala. Three Iraqi trucks were reported burned at the Al-Yarubiyah border crossing between Iraq and Syria.

GULF STATES
Kuwait's armed forces intercepted two ballistic missiles and 13 drones launched from Iran; no damage or casualties were reported, though some power outages were attributed to air defense operations. Bahrain reported sirens and aerial interceptions. An official from the UAE reportedly warned Iran would "pay a heavy price." The US issued a warning to Gulf states to prepare for a possible Iranian response. Qatar's Foreign Ministry summoned the Iranian Deputy Ambassador to file a formal complaint regarding an attack on a Qatari tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, demanding an immediate halt to actions affecting regional security and freedom of navigation. The Foreign Ministers of Oman and Saudi Arabia discussed the security of maritime routes and freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. Yemen's Foreign Ministry announced full support for Iran against foreign aggression, condemning recent US attacks. Shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has "practically stopped," with only four tankers reported to have passed through today, and shipping insurance premiums have surged 30-80 times their normal rate, now costing $3-8 million per large tanker.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Extensive US Strikes on Iran:** The US military conducted over 80 strikes against Iranian military targets in the southern provinces, including Bandar Abbas and Bushehr, in response to Iranian attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.
2.  **Iranian Casualties and Retaliation:** Eight Iranian Army servicemen were martyred in the US strikes. In response, the IRGC claimed to have attacked 85 US military targets in Bahrain and Kuwait, and Kuwait confirmed intercepting 2 ballistic missiles and 13 drones from Iran.
3.  **Threat to Close Strait of Hormuz:** Iran announced a new strategy, vowing to fully close the Strait of Hormuz and retaliate with at least twice the number of targets hit if new attacks occur. Shipping through the Strait is reported to have "practically stopped."
4.  **US Revokes Iran Oil Waiver:** The Trump administration officially revoked Iran's sanctions waiver for oil production and sales, citing Iranian actions in the Strait of Hormuz as a direct violation of the interim agreement.
5.  **US Declares Interim Agreement "Over":** President Trump stated he believes the interim agreement with Iran is "over," labeled further negotiations a "waste of time," and threatened additional strikes, a naval blockade, and the occupation of Kharg Island.
6.  **Hezbollah Clash in Lebanon:** An Israeli Oketz canine unit dog was killed by a Hezbollah gunman in Bint Jbeil, southern Lebanon, before the gunman was eliminated by Israeli forces. The IDF is investigating the precise details of the engagement.
7.  **Shin Bet Chief Controversy:** Leaked recordings revealed Israeli Shin Bet Chief David Zini emphasizing his loyalty to "the elected official" and criticizing the legal system, prompting significant political backlash and support.
8.  **Qatari Formal Complaint:** Qatar summoned Iran's Deputy Ambassador to formally complain about an attack on a Qatari tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, demanding an explanation and an immediate cessation of actions impacting maritime security.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are extremely high following direct military exchanges and explicit threats from both the US and Iran. The mutual declaration of the interim agreement's termination further destabilizes the situation. Active flashpoints include the Strait of Hormuz, where Iranian threats of closure and US threats of naval blockade could lead to a direct naval confrontation, and southern Iran, which is experiencing ongoing US airstrikes and Iranian retaliation. The Lebanon-Israel border remains tense with low-level engagements. Military postures have shifted, with the US executing sustained "powerful strikes," US warnings to Gulf states to brace for Iranian responses, and Israel actively preparing for a "new confrontation" or "full war" with Iran, in close coordination with CENTCOM. Red lines for Iran include new attacks on its territory or attempts to control the Strait of Hormuz, while for the US, continued attacks on commercial shipping and advancements in Iran's nuclear program are critical. This environment presents a significant potential for rapid and widespread regional escalation.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The US posture is highly confrontational, with President Trump explicitly terminating the interim agreement with Iran and threatening severe further military action, including occupying Kharg Island and reimposing a naval blockade. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth cancelled a scheduled visit to Israel, indicating readiness for "deeper" attacks on Iran. Despite this, a US official stated that Washington intends to continue negotiations in good faith. Trump met with Syrian President Al-Shara, suggesting potential removal of Syria from the terror list in exchange for assistance with Hezbollah.
Gulf States, including Qatar, Oman, and Saudi Arabia, have expressed concern over maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar issued a formal diplomatic complaint to Iran following an attack on its tanker. The UAE issued a stark warning that Iran would "pay a heavy price." Kuwait reported intercepting Iranian projectiles.
European nations have largely condemned Iran's actions. French President Macron and German Chancellor Mertens stated that Iran violated the interim agreement, while UK Prime Minister Starmer called for a return to a ceasefire. German Foreign Minister Wadephul called for de-escalation and a return to negotiations, suggesting European countries could assist in mine clearing in Hormuz. Italian Prime Minister Meloni expressed hope for negotiations, doubting the effectiveness of military options.
China's Ambassador to Iran emphasized support for a return to normal conditions in Hormuz and respect for Iran's legitimate rights. Turkey's President Erdogan, at the NATO summit, thanked certain countries for air defense aid during the "war in Iran," and reports suggest the US may condition F-35 sales to Turkey on the deactivation of its S-400 systems. NATO Secretary-General Rutte affirmed strong unity within the alliance and described US attacks on Iran as "absolutely necessary" and "totally crucial."

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions and unverified claims exist. The CNN report of a US strike hitting a school and causing nearly 200 casualties, with commanders bypassing outdated intelligence warnings, is a severe allegation requiring independent verification, particularly given CENTCOM's detailed list of military targets. IRGC's claim of downing an MQ-9 drone lacks independent confirmation. Reports of Hormozgan airport closures were directly contradicted by Iranian civil aviation authorities. US President Trump's statement about Iran killing 54,000 protesters and his often inflammatory rhetoric should be viewed as politically charged and unverified. The varying accounts of the Bint Jbeil Hezbollah gunman's killing by IDF forces ("good-faith human error" admitted by IDF) indicate a reporting gap or internal discrepancy. There is also an apparent disconnect between Trump's public pronouncements about the "interim agreement" being "over" and US officials stating an intent to continue "good faith" negotiations, which may reflect a distinction between different diplomatic tracks or simply rhetorical strategy. The exact details of the "Islamabad MoU" and its precise violations by both sides remain largely undefined in the provided raw intelligence.
